title: Welcome to Python
body: Python is a readable, versatile programming language. You can use it to automate everyday tasks, analyze data, and build applications. In this lesson, you’ll write your very first Python program.
code:
# Your first Python program
print("Hello, ShimentoX!")
task: The print() function displays a message. Put your text inside quotation marks, then place it inside the parentheses.

title: Variables & data types
body: Variables give names to values so you can use them later. Python understands common types such as strings, integers, floats, and booleans.
code:
employee = "Alex"
courses_completed = 1
learning_hours = 2.5
is_learning = True

print(employee)
task: Try naming a variable for your learning goal. Use descriptive names and underscores between words.

title: Working with strings
body: A string is a sequence of characters. Combine strings, change their case, or insert variables with an f-string.
task: An f-string starts with f before the quote. Expressions inside braces are replaced with their values.

title: Lists & collections
body: Lists keep multiple values together in order. You can add values, access an item by its position, and find the length of the list.
task: Python counts positions from zero. The first element is at index 0.

title: Conditions & loops
body: Conditions help a program make decisions. Loops repeat an action for each item in a collection.
task: Indentation groups statements together. Use four spaces for each level.

title: Functions & your next steps
body: Functions group reusable instructions under a name. Use parameters to give a function input and return to send a result back.
task: You’ve covered the foundations. Practice by writing a function that turns hours into minutes. Keep building your Python skills!
